items.title: Out-of-control fire rages at one of Australia's two oil refineries
items.description: Authorities were called to one of Australia's two operational oil refineries around 11pm after residents reported "explosions and flames".

items.title: Albanese government's frustration rises as Australians pay price for war
items.description: Fuel prices and inflation aren't the only metrics climbing as the Strait of Hormuz remains shut. The Albanese government's level of frustration is rising just as fast.

items.title: Creators of fuel dashboard quoted by News Corp have links to Liberals
items.description: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation raises questions about popular independent fuel security dashboards that have emerged online, including one whose creators are linked to the Liberal Party.

items.title: Live: Trump says Iran war 'close to over', Israel continues strikes on Hezbollah
items.description: The US president has said a deal with Iran is "preferable" and to expect an "amazing two days" ahead. Follow live.

items.title: Iran briefing with Matthew Doran: There could be respite for Lebanon despite Netanyahu's latest orders
items.description: Israeli forces are expected to "overwhelm" parts of southern Lebanon and yet a ceasefire may still be only a matter of days away.

items.title: Ukraine looking to 'capitalise' on new momentum against Russia
items.description: Western officials and analysts say Ukrainian forces have disrupted Russia's planned spring offensive and managed to retake territory.

items.title: At least nine dead, including eight children, in Türkiye school shooting
items.description: A boy, believed to be aged about 13, carried out the shooting in southeastern Türkiye, killing his fellow students and a teacher. It is the second school shooting in the country in two days.

items.title: Dozens of workers with disability made redundant by award-winning charity
items.description: Help Enterprises made 41 positions redundant weeks after being named Brisbane's social enterprise of the year.

items.title: Proposal to block non-citizens from first homebuyer scheme slammed
items.description: Multicultural groups are concerned Angus Taylor's proposal to prevent permanent residents from accessing the Australian Government 5% Deposit Scheme could deter skilled migrants from coming to Australia.

items.title: 'Canary in coal mine' warning as marine pest found in new area
items.description: The discovery on Tasmania's west coast has scientists and fishers alike fearing the spread of a destructive species to another previously untouched part of the state's marine environment.

items.title: Short-stay levy overperforms, as holiday rental growth stagnates in Victoria
items.description: Data suggests the growth in short-stay accommodation listings in Victoria has slowed in the year after the Victorian government's new tax came into effect.

items.title: Councils become insurers as premiums rise by 500pc
items.description: Adam Osborne was quoted a staggering $60,000 for his home insurance this year. With others in the same boat, six Queensland councils are looking at creating their own insurance mutual to drive down premiums.

items.title: Defence spending to climb by $53 billion as 'international norms' erode
items.description: Australia's defence spending will climb by $53 billion over the next decade amid what the federal government says are "intensifying" global risks.

items.title: American YouTuber jailed in South Korea for being a public nuisance
items.description: A Seoul court found Johnny Somali displayed “severe” disrespect for South Korean law over a series of provocative stunts he live-streamed.

items.title: How AI might mean you pay more — or less — for fashion online
items.description: Dynamic pricing is already changing the final cost of clothing. Some prices are rising, but others are falling.

items.title: Quiz: Can you tell the different between The Pitt and E.R.?
items.description: Ahead of The Pitt season finale dropping this week, can you pick the difference between it and its hospital drama ancestor E.R.?

items.title: How this tiny town welcomed a 70-piece orchestra
items.description: The Sydney Youth Orchestras travelled to this tiny town to help inspire the local kids, but when they left, they were the ones who felt changed.

items.title: Henderson 'content' knowing her epic reign will not last forever
items.description: Rebecca Henderson has won 13 elite national mountain bike cross-country titles in a row and, this season, is unbeaten in the UCI Oceania Continental series, which concludes this weekend at the Cairns Rainforest Rumble.

items.title: Taylor's migration plan doesn't make much sense. It doesn't have to
items.description: More than a day after Angus Taylor unveiled the first plank of the Coalition's long-awaited migration policy and many media interviews later, it's still unclear what the opposition is actually proposing to change.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade could turn into global agrifood crisis
items.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations says ships in the Strait of Hormuz need to start moving again to avoid a global agrifood crisis. Here's why.

items.title: How the technology we use every day is changing our brains
items.description: If it feels harder to concentrate than it used to, it's not just you. Scientists say your brain is reacting exactly as it was designed to — but in a very different world.

items.title: Farmer feels 'disrespected' over VicGrid's attempt to access land
items.description: VicGrid escalates its attempts to access land for VNI West surveys, threatening fines or court-ordered entry to farmers who stand in the way.

items.title: Teen admits creating deepfakes in Australian-first prosecution
items.description: An Adelaide teenager who was the first person charged under new nationwide laws aimed at tackling adult deepfake pornography has pleaded guilty to two counts of creating or altering sexual material without consent.

items.title: 'Your courage does not end': Prince Harry addresses room of veterans in Canberra
items.description: The Duke of Sussex flew solo to the nation's capital and addressed an Invictus Australia event at the Australian War Memorial.

items.title: Media boss's wife feared she would die, tore his clothing during alleged attack, court told
items.description: The wife of media executive Antony Catalano fled the couple's luxury apartment and flagged down a passing car for help following a sustained attack by her husband that caused hospitalisation, police allege.
